prompt: An investor wants to know whether the electric scooter rental industry is attractive. The candidate's framework: (1) Revenue: price and volume; (2) Fixed costs; (3) Variable costs. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 2 and 3 overlap: charging and repairs are both fixed and variable
options.feedback: Charging and repairs are variable costs; the split is clean. The issue is that a company profit tree can't judge an industry.

options.text: Missing: how fast the scooters wear out
options.feedback: Scooter life matters, but adding a cost line doesn't fix the mismatch.

options.text: Bucket 2 doesn't belong: scooter companies rent their fleets
options.feedback: Nothing says fleets are rented, and fixed costs matter. The issue is the generic framework.

options.text: It's a generic profit tree: it can't judge a whole industry's outlook
options.feedback: Right. Industry attractiveness needs market growth, competition, unit economics per ride and regulation.

explanation: Whether an industry is attractive depends on growth, competition, economics per ride and regulation, not one company's revenue and costs.

extras.corrected_framework: Market size and growth; competition and pricing power; unit economics per ride; regulation and city permits
